questions.stem: Which vessels carry blood away from the heart?

options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.
Veins return blood toward the heart.
Venules collect blood between capillaries and veins.
They return tissue fluid, pumping no blood from the heart.

questions.stem: Which vessel breaks the rule that arteries carry oxygenated blood?

options.explanation: It is a vein, not an artery.
Right — the other options each misplace a concept.
The aorta carries oxygenated blood outward.
It carries oxygenated blood to the kidneys.

questions.stem: Which pair of vessels connects toward the liver?

options.explanation: The hepatic vein carries blood away from the liver.
Those belong to the kidneys.

options.text: The hepatic artery and the hepatic portal vein
options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.
The portal vein also runs toward it, carrying digested food.

questions.stem: What sequence describes the narrowing and widening between heart and organ?

options.text: Artery to venule to capillary to vein
options.explanation: Arterioles come before capillaries, not venules.
That reverses the one-way loop.
Arteries branch into arterioles, not the reverse.

options.text: Artery to arteriole to capillary to venule to vein
options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.

questions.stem: What role do the lymphatic vessels play alongside the blood circulation?

options.text: They collect excess tissue fluid and return it to the circulatory system
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.

options.text: They carry oxygen to the lungs
options.explanation: The pulmonary vessels do that.

options.text: They pump blood faster than arteries
options.explanation: They carry fluid, not blood, and without a pump.

options.text: They remove blood from the body
options.explanation: Nothing removes blood; the loop is closed.

questions.stem: Name the vessels bringing blood toward the heart and toward the lungs.
questions.modelAnswer: The vena cava and pulmonary vein bring blood toward the heart, and the pulmonary artery carries it toward the lungs.

questions.stem: State which vessel carries blood away from the kidneys.
questions.modelAnswer: The renal vein carries blood away from the kidneys.

questions.stem: Explain why the pulmonary vessels are called the exception pair.
questions.modelAnswer: Because each breaks its family's oxygen rule: the artery carries deoxygenated blood and the vein carries oxygenated blood, opposite to every other vessel of its kind.

questions.stem: A diagram labels four vessels at the liver but mixes two from the kidneys. Identify the liver set.
questions.modelAnswer: The liver set is the hepatic artery and hepatic portal vein toward it with the hepatic vein away; the renal artery and vein belong to the kidneys.
